# eslint-plugin-mongodb-security

Guide for AI coding assistants using this plugin in a project. To change the plugin's own source, read https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/blob/main/AGENTS.md instead.

> ESLint MongoDB security rules for MongoDB and Mongoose — detects NoSQL operator injection, unsafe queries and regex, hardcoded connection strings, and missing TLS.

## Enable it

```bash
npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-mongodb-security
```

Requires ESLint ^8.40.0 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0 and Node >=22.13.0.

Flat config files (`eslint.config.*`) are found by ESLint 8.57 and newer; on ESLint 9 and 10 they are the default.

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import mongodbSecurity from 'eslint-plugin-mongodb-security';

export default [mongodbSecurity.configs.recommended];
```

Each preset is one flat config object: put it in the array as an element, do not spread it. Rule ids are prefixed `mongodb-security/`. Add it to the config you already have; do not remove other plugins. TypeScript files need a TypeScript parser in the config (`typescript-eslint`).

Use it alongside `eslint-plugin-security`, not instead of it: keep that plugin if the project has it. Measured overlap and the limits of both: https://eslint.interlace.tools/docs/getting-started/with-eslint-plugin-security

## Presets

| Preset        | Rules | Errors | Warnings |
| ------------- | ----- | ------ | -------- |
| `flagship`    | 1     | 1      | 0        |
| `recommended` | 14    | 8      | 6        |
| `strict`      | 16    | 16     | 0        |
| `mongoose`    | 9     | 8      | 1        |

### `flagship`

1 rule:

- `no-unsafe-query` (error): Prevent NoSQL injection via direct use of user input in MongoDB queries.

### `recommended`

14 rules:

- `no-unsafe-query` (error): Prevent NoSQL injection via direct use of user input in MongoDB queries.
- `no-operator-injection` (error): Prevent MongoDB operator injection attacks via user input.
- `no-unsafe-where` (error): Prevent $where operator RCE attacks (CVE-2025-23061).
- `no-unsafe-regex-query` (error): Prevent ReDoS attacks via $regex with user input.
- `no-hardcoded-connection-string` (error): Prevent hardcoded MongoDB connection strings with credentials.
- `no-hardcoded-credentials` (error): Prevent hardcoded MongoDB authentication credentials.
- `require-tls-connection` (warn): Require TLS for MongoDB connections in production.
- `require-auth-mechanism` (warn): Require explicit authentication mechanism (SCRAM-SHA-256).
- `require-schema-validation` (warn): Require validation on Mongoose schema fields.
- `no-select-sensitive-fields` (warn): Prevent returning sensitive fields like password in queries.
- `no-bypass-middleware` (warn): Prevent bypassing Mongoose pre/post middleware hooks.
- `no-unsafe-populate` (error): Prevent user-controlled populate() paths (CVE-2025-23061).
- `no-unbounded-find` (warn): Require limit() on find queries to prevent resource exhaustion.
- `no-debug-mode-production` (error): Prevent Mongoose debug mode in production.

### `strict`

Everything in `recommended` plus 2 more (some shared rules run at a different severity here):

- `require-projection` (error): Require field projection on MongoDB queries.
- `require-lean-queries` (error): Suggest .lean() for read-only Mongoose queries.

### `mongoose`

9 rules:

- `no-unsafe-query` (error): Prevent NoSQL injection via direct use of user input in MongoDB queries.
- `no-operator-injection` (error): Prevent MongoDB operator injection attacks via user input.
- `no-unsafe-where` (error): Prevent $where operator RCE attacks (CVE-2025-23061).
- `require-schema-validation` (error): Require validation on Mongoose schema fields.
- `no-select-sensitive-fields` (error): Prevent returning sensitive fields like password in queries.
- `no-bypass-middleware` (error): Prevent bypassing Mongoose pre/post middleware hooks.
- `no-unsafe-populate` (error): Prevent user-controlled populate() paths (CVE-2025-23061).
- `require-lean-queries` (warn): Suggest .lean() for read-only Mongoose queries.
- `no-debug-mode-production` (error): Prevent Mongoose debug mode in production.

## Other Interlace plugins by dependency

If the project also depends on one of these, add the matching plugin the same way:

- `express`, `fastify`, `koa`, `@hapi/hapi`, `restify`, `hono`, `next`, `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/common`, `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`, `commander`, `yargs`, `@oclif/core`, `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-node-security`
- `express`: `eslint-plugin-express-security`
- `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`: `eslint-plugin-nestjs-security`
- `react`, `react-dom`, `preact`, `vue`, `svelte`, `@angular/core`, `solid-js`, `lit`, `next`, `nuxt`: `eslint-plugin-browser-security`
- `jsonwebtoken`, `jose`, `express-jwt`, `@nestjs/jwt`, `jwks-rsa`, `jwt-decode`: `eslint-plugin-jwt-security`
- `pg`, `pg-pool`, `pg-promise`, `postgres`, `slonik`: `eslint-plugin-postgresql-security`
- `mysql2`, `mysql`: `eslint-plugin-mysql-security`
- `better-sqlite3`, `sqlite3`: `eslint-plugin-sqlite-security`
- `knex`: `eslint-plugin-knex-security`
- `@prisma/client`, `prisma`: `eslint-plugin-prisma-security`
- `drizzle-orm`: `eslint-plugin-drizzle-security`
- `sequelize`: `eslint-plugin-sequelize-security`
- `typeorm`: `eslint-plugin-typeorm-security`
- `@supabase/supabase-js`: `eslint-plugin-supabase-security`
- `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-mcp-sdk-security`
- `openai`, `@openai/agents`: `eslint-plugin-openai-security`
- `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`: `eslint-plugin-anthropic-security`
- `@google/genai`: `eslint-plugin-gemini-security`
- `ai`: `eslint-plugin-vercel-ai-security`
- `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`: `eslint-plugin-lambda-security`

The full stack-to-plugin playbook (with config rendering and a proof step) is the `security-linting` skill: https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/tree/main/skills/security-linting
